slides.text: They gave me the time machine to prevent World War III. I was supposed to go back to 2024 and stop a rogue general. But on my way to the coordinates, I walked past a McDonald’s and remembered something tragic. In 2004, they discontinued the Szechuan sauce. I looked at the ticking temporal device on my wrist. I had time. Just a quick pit stop to grab a ten-piece nugget.

I emerged in a 2004 drive-thru, wearing a futuristic silver spacesuit. The teenager at the window stared at me. 'I need all your Szechuan sauce,' I demanded, slapping a chunk of pure gold onto the counter. He nervously handed me a massive cardboard box full of packets. I felt like a god. But when I turned around, the space-time portal had closed. I forgot to recharge the temporal battery.

Fast forward twenty years. I never stopped the rogue general, and the apocalypse happened. The world is a radioactive wasteland. I currently live in an underground bunker with a mutant badger named Kevin. But honestly? I’m thriving. The other survivors are eating canned beans and rad-roaches, while Kevin and I are dipping everything into perfectly preserved, vintage Szechuan sauce. History is all about priorities.
